story.title: A whole crab, to begin
story.letter: The crab arrives with both claws and all its sideways opinions. Send this first shape as it is. A moved claw has its own envelope.
story.sentCaption: The whole crab has been sent.

story.title: The claw writes from below
story.letter: One claw has moved beneath the shell. The smaller one stays high, as if the address and the reply were written on different lines.
story.sentCaption: The lower claw found its line.

story.title: Beside the shoulder
story.letter: The crab has shifted part of its shell sideways. The snail offers a low shoulder. Put the two beside each other without asking either to straighten up.
story.goal: Make and send Sideways Neighbour and Snail Shoulder.
story.sentCaption: The shifted shell and small shoulder travelled together.

story.title: A visit with the coil undone
story.letter: The snail has opened its outer whorl behind its head. Send the low crab claw along for the visit. A little company can leave a large curve quite unclosed.
story.goal: Make and send Claw Correspondence and Uncoiled Visit.
story.sentCaption: The open whorl kept its own shape, with company beside it.

story.title: The handle end of the task
story.letter: Here is a can with somewhere to hold it and somewhere to pour. Send the whole small arrangement before either end changes its mind.
story.goal: Make and send Garden Watering Can.

story.title: A rose brought low
story.letter: The rose has moved down beside the can. No water needs to fall; the lowered spout is already a small act of attention.
story.sentCaption: The rose took the lower place.

story.title: Tools at the edge
story.letter: The can lowers its rose while the trowel moves its scoop off to one side. They look ready to attend to the margin rather than the middle.
story.goal: Make and send Lowered Rose and Trowel Offset.
story.sentCaption: The two tools found the margin.

story.title: Where the hand would go
story.letter: The can has raised one shoulder but left its handle low. The trowel keeps its grip above its scoop. Two ordinary places for a hand have become rather different pictures.
story.goal: Make and send Can of Two Heights and Garden Trowel.
story.sentCaption: The raised can and the whole trowel have been sent.

story.title: A scoop visits the first garden
story.letter: The trowel opens its scoop toward the old Fern Cup. The garden has come in its own container. Perhaps tending begins by noticing what is already there.
story.goal: Make and send Opened Scoop and Fern Cup.
story.sentCaption: The opened scoop visited the Fern Cup. This little tending is complete.

story.title: A weight for the corner
story.letter: The flatiron has brought its broad sole and a handle raised above it. Send its whole weight on paper; the envelope will manage.
story.sentCaption: The flatiron arrived without weighing down the envelope.

story.title: Room at the heel
story.letter: A notch has divided the iron’s heel into two blunt ends. The pointed front stays together. Even a firm shape can leave something unsaid at the back.
story.goal: Make and send Flatiron Forked Heel.
story.sentCaption: The forked heel left its small omission.

story.title: Cloth takes a bend
story.letter: The mitten bends at its middle beside the iron’s forked heel. The soft piece has not been pressed straight. It may have a better use for its elbow.
story.goal: Make and send Flatiron Forked Heel and Mitten Elbow.
story.sentCaption: The cloth kept its bend beside the iron.

story.title: Under the lifted seam
story.letter: The handled iron lifts away from its sole along one seam. The whole mitten waits beside that opening. Let the heavy picture make the larger gesture this time.
story.goal: Make and send Flatiron Lifted Seam and Paper Mitten.
story.sentCaption: The iron lifted its seam; the mitten stayed whole.

story.title: The inside of the regards
story.letter: The mitten has turned its cuff down one side, showing the pale reverse. This last reply needs only the cloth. There is another side to a warm regard.
story.goal: Make and send Turned Mitten Cuff.
story.sentCaption: The turned cuff closed the letter with its reverse showing.

story.title: The figure shifts its footing
story.letter: The knight’s base stays broad while the horse has moved to its edge. Send the offset figure. Its whole, unshifted relation to the base has a separate letter.
story.goal: Make and send Knight Side Step.
story.sentCaption: The knight arrived at the edge of its base.

story.title: What the figure stands on
story.letter: The horse and pedestal are still one solid picture here. Give the whole knight a reply too. The support has been present from the beginning.
story.goal: Make and send Paper Chess Knight.
story.sentCaption: The whole knight brought its pedestal.

story.title: One tooth writes separately
story.letter: One tooth has moved outward from the cogwheel, still attached by a paper tongue. The first answer from this wheel is a small departure.
story.goal: Make and send Cogwheel Missing Beat.
story.sentCaption: The displaced tooth sent the first answer.

story.title: Teeth, with a leaf between
story.letter: Send that displaced cog tooth to the old Frond Key. The key has teeth too, and has somehow found room for a leaf. Their resemblance is a reason for a letter, not a lock to solve.
story.goal: Make and send Cogwheel Missing Beat and Frond Key.
story.sentCaption: The cogwheel found teeth and a leaf in its reply.

story.title: Back to the supporting cast
story.letter: The cogwheel opens its two sectors into a broad angular jaw. Return the offset knight beside it: one picture opens, the other still has somewhere to stand. That is enough for this exchange.
story.goal: Make and send Knight Side Step and Cogwheel Half Turn.
story.sentCaption: The jaw and the offset knight closed these four correspondences.

sideways-company.title: Sideways Company
sideways-company.opening: Two crab letters begin this envelope. Answer both to meet the snail; then two different visits wait together.
sideways-company.ending: The two visits have arrived. Neither animal had to become the other to share an envelope.
sideways-company.goal: Send every story letter in Sideways Company. Supplies are free; purchases and optional discoveries are not required.
sideways-company.sourceNotice: Both opening story letters unlock Paper Snail. A previously earned source remains selected alongside the first new source.

postscripts.caption: The claws turn inward around a low, solid shell.
postscripts.reverse: The claws turn around their own shell. This crab has found a boundary it can carry, with a gap left for company.
postscripts.rewardPolicy: No reward; discovery only; do not consume or require delivery.
postscripts.presentationContract: Show the reverse only after this exact piece is discovered. Use existing single-picture discovery/postcard surfaces. No combined layout, implied companion discovery, chapter completion or volume completion.

upgradeDecision: No new sorters or prices in this tranche. The mandatory work is deliberately short, and all eight tier-five routes are optional. Do not pad letters to justify shop purchases. Existing earned and available upgrades, prices, purchase ledgers and output cursors are preserved; existing Fern/Key sorters can shorten callbacks. Optional spending cannot gate story.
tierOneRewardDecision: The four untransformed introductory pieces and the two tier-one companions carry zero additional XP/coins. Each mixed letter earns the unchanged tier2–5 rewards of its other piece. Direct authored requirements are used; do not call target/rewardsFor for tier1. No legacy reward table changes.

boundary.entryCopy: The first twenty-four chapters are complete. Four more envelopes bring forty new pictures. Open them when you want to continue; your finished letters and saved table stay with you.
